newsitem.title: USA: "Wired" building to open in London.
newsitem.headline: "Wired" building to open in London.

text.p: The owner and developer of a "wired" building offering tenants turbocharged Internet access and other leading-edge features Tuesday announced plans to convert a former 1920s cigarette factory in London into another high-tech mecca.

The London Information Technology Center/Carreras in central London's Camden Town section is intended to be the first in a series of "smart" buildings around the world and will be electronically linked to its New York counterpart, said John Gilbert, chief operating officer of developer Rudin Management Co. Inc.

"The concept of 'picking up the phone' has been revolutionised by the ability to 'just plug in,' which enables businesses to reach worldwide partners with information from simple documents to live video in seconds," company President Bill Rudin said in a statement.

Plans for the Carreras building, a huge structure modelled on ancient Egyptian temple architecture, were unveiled at a joint video news conference at the New York Information Technology Centre in Manhattan's financial district and at the London Business School.

The building will be equipped with a high-speed connection to the Internet, fiber optic cable, satellite links, a video wall display, video conferencing and other high-tech features similar to those in the New York centre. It is expected to open in August 1997.
The developer and owner of the London building is Kian Gwa PLC of Bangkok, Thailand. Gilbert said the cost of the renovation was not yet known.
The 500,000-square-foot building was erected in 1928 as a cigarette factory. It was converted to offices in the early 1960s and has parking space for 147 cars.

Co-Chairman Lewis Rudin said in a statement that the New York technology centre had helped Lower Manhattan's "Silicon Alley" by drawing attention to the area and creating a climate for residential and commercial development to make it a 24-hour community.
"Now, we go global and do for London what we have done for New York City," he said.
